gaps: G1: decision doc says 'cancelled' but the schema/type union spells it 'canceled' — a sweep matching the doc spelling would silently delete nothing.
G2: ended_at is only set at terminal settle; a legacy row without it would never age out.
G3: syncAllJobs runs every 60s and on every requestSync — a naive hook would seq-scan the table far too often.
G4: a required new scheduler callback breaks 26 existing test fixtures.
G5: no index covers the delete predicate; first sweep after deploy could be a long transaction.
contradictions: C1: 'run from existing maintenance machinery' vs 'the only hook fires every 60s' — the mechanism exists but its cadence does not fit a retention sweep.
resolutions: G1: sweep filters on the typed union values ('completed','failed','canceled'); the integration test seeds all three so a spelling regression fails loudly.
G2: age column is coalesce(ended_at, updated_at) — both NOT NULL paths covered.
G4: the sweep is an OPTIONAL injected dep beside hasLiveAdmissionBacklog, defaulted in scheduler.ts — zero fixture edits.

G5: batched deletes (id IN subselect LIMIT 5000) bound each transaction; no index added deliberately — table is bounded post-retention and the ceiling+upgrade path (partial ended_at index) is recorded in the plan.
G3: per-process last-sweep timestamp caps execution at once per 6h; the 60s tick merely checks the guard.
C1: resolved by the same guard — the existing machinery hosts the sweep, the guard supplies the retention-appropriate cadence, so no new timer/subsystem is added.
summary: PERF-4 plan grill: 5 gaps + 1 contradiction, all resolved; policy fixed by accepted decision 0103, no open user choices.
